drivingQuestion: What does R' Eliezer derive from 'shall not be credited', which Aḥerim use to show disqualification by intent?
outcomeNote: R' Eliezer uses the phrase for R' Yannai's rule; Rav Mari's lashes version is identified with R' Yehuda

segments.he: אֲחֵרִים אוֹמְרִים: בְּמַחְשָׁבָה הוּא נִפְסָל, וְאֵינוֹ נִפְסָל בִּשְׁלִישִׁי. וְרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר – ״לֹא יֵחָשֵׁב״ מַאי עָבֵיד לֵיהּ?
segments.en: § The baraita stated that «Aḥerim say:» The phrase “neither shall it be credited” indicates that the offering «is disqualified by» improper «intention, and it is not disqualified» by consumption beyond its designated time «on the third» day. The Gemara asks: «And Rabbi Eliezer,» who derives this halakha from a different source, «what does he do with» the phrase «“neither shall it be credited”?»

segments.he: מִיבְּעֵי לֵיהּ לְכִדְרַבִּי יַנַּאי – דְּאָמַר רַבִּי יַנַּאי: מִנַּיִן לְמַחְשָׁבוֹת שֶׁמּוֹצִיאוֹת זוֹ מִזּוֹ? שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״לֹא יֵחָשֵׁב״ – לֹא יְעָרֵב בּוֹ מַחְשָׁבוֹת אֲחֵרוֹת.
segments.en: The Gemara responds: «He requires it for» that «which Rabbi Yannai» says, «as Rabbi Yannai says: From where» is it derived «with regard to intentions that they displace one another,» i.e., that an additional improper intention prevents the offering from being rendered piggul? «As it is stated: “Neither shall it be credited [yeḥashev],”» indicating that an offering is rendered piggul only if the priest does «not mix other» improper «intentions [maḥashavot] with» intent of piggul.

segments.he: וְרַב מָרִי מַתְנֵי, אָמַר רַבִּי יַנַּאי: מִנַּיִן לִמְחַשֵּׁב בְּקָדָשִׁים שֶׁהוּא לוֹקֶה? תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: ״לֹא יֵחָשֵׁב״.
segments.en: «And Rav Mari teaches» that «Rabbi Yannai says: From where» is it derived «that one who has» improper «intentions with regard to sacrificial» animals «is flogged» like one who transgressed a prohibition? «The verse states: “Neither shall it be credited [lo yeḥashev],”» i.e., one reads the verse as if it states: One shall not have improper intention [lo y’ḥashev].

segments.he: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אָשֵׁי לְרַב מָרִי: לָאו שֶׁאֵין בּוֹ מַעֲשֶׂה הוּא, וְכׇל לָאו שֶׁאֵין בּוֹ מַעֲשֶׂה – אֵין לוֹקִין עָלָיו! אֲמַר לֵיהּ: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה הִיא, דְּאָמַר: לָאו שֶׁאֵין בּוֹ מַעֲשֶׂה – לוֹקִין עָלָיו.
segments.en: «Rav Ashi said to Rav Mari:» But «it is a prohibition that does not involve an action, and» the principle is that «for» transgressing «any prohibition that does not involve an action one is not flogged.» Rav Mari «said to him: It is» in accordance with the opinion of «Rabbi Yehuda, who says: For» transgressing «a prohibition that does not involve an action one is flogged.»
